title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-03
content:
Morning notes / running todo list - GPU ops

Quick context:
- Today: free up capacity for dedicated customers (batch jobs up next week)
- Cluster: prod-gpu-us-west (32 nodes, mix A100-80GB + A40 nodes). We need ~10% headroom for spikes.

Top priorities:
- [ ] INFRA-4123: Finish drain+cordon script for A40 nodes (warming up) -> blocked by kernel module unload issue on node pool 3
  - root cause: nvidia driver 535.x doesn't like hot-unplug path for MIG config change
  - todo: test kernel-compat branch from PR #287 on 3 staging nodes (Maya to help)
- [ ] Run capacity sweep for March deploy: target reserved slots for dedicated pools -> numbers below
  - current available GPU slots (prod): 256 (A100-80) + 120 (A40 equiv) -> normalize to vGPU units = 256*4 + 120*1 = 1144 units (approx)
  - target reserved for Dedicated: 20% -> 229 units (round up 240)
  - action: update autoscaler policy and quota config; verify RBAC for quota controllers
- [ ] Validate NFS mount stability for /var/kvcache on inference nodes (random disconnects overnight)
  - symptoms: 2 OOM pods, kernel dmesg shows stale filehandle errors -> likely NFS server maintenance window overlap
  - workaround: bump liveness probe timeout to 60s for kvcache sidecar until we fix server maintenance schedule

Investigations in-progress:
- KV cache evictions spike during 00:00-01:00 UTC — correlates with nightly backup job (backup-service/api-db). Need to coordinate with SRE.
  - temp fix: set cache TTL shorter for non-critical models to reduce memory pressure
- Latency tail on short prompts on A100-80GB since rolling kernel update (noticed 99p latency +14%)
  - hypothesis: driver/kernel combo -> test rollback to 534.x on 2 canary nodes
  - alert: add metric "inference.kernel.rollback_needed" to sprint board if rollback reduces 99p by >10%

Operational runbook notes (todo to formalize):
- Node drain checklist for A40 pool:
  1) cordon node
  2) migrate long-running infer pods to A100 pool with migrate flag
  3) run /usr/local/bin/unload-nvidia-modules -> watch for failure code 42 -> if fails escalate to kernel-team
  4) reboot -> verify docker+nvidia runtime start
  5) run smoke gen test (small prompts 8-16 tokens x100)

Reminders / quick hits:
- Ping @oncall in #gpu-ops Slack after deploying driver change (include sample logs): attach dmesg + nvidia-smi output
- Add ticket to backlog: audit quantized model assignments per node type (A100 vs A40) -> some 4-bit models shouldn't be on A40 by default
- Update cost model after reserving 20% dedicated capacity (finance review on Friday)

Short-term checklist (today):
- [ ] Deploy PR #287 to staging-3 and run smoke test (owner: Alex)
- [ ] Create INFRA-4198 for NFS server maintenance window update (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Update autoscaler policy JSON and create rollout (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Slack note to SRE: pause nightly db backup between 23:30-01:30 UTC tomorrow

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep a copy of the drain script in /home/alex/gpu-ops/drain-scripts -> check in once stable
- When we run the capacity sweep, include tail-latency buckets by model family (chat vs short-complete vs embeddings)
- Consider pre-warming KV cache for top-10 models before expected traffic windows (experiment with prefix caching TTL=2h)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are Dedicated customers ok w/ reserved capacity that forces occasional routing to hosted fallback? need product sign-off
- Does billing team want per-vGPU charge or per-slot? affects reserve math

End-of-day note: if drain script still fails after PR deploy -> plan B is rolling-replace node pool with images pinned to 534.x driver. Will coordinate with release-engineering.

-- Alex
